reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor established four things I had wrong: (a) my exit P/E mixed EME (with EPS not on the cited page) into a revenue-weighted median; on the whole-company median (MTZ 16.6, PWR 35.2, PRIM 17.1, MYRG 20.2 = 18.65x) and DY's own 12.13x, k = 0.8 gives 13.2x (revenue-weighting with the corrected Building Systems peers gives the same 18.62x). (b) Supplier finance does not bear interest, so I moved it out of net debt; my own AP-days test against the four pre-program quarters (18.40 days vs 27.67 now) makes 204.3 debt-like, an equity adjustment. (c) I counted SBC twice; shares now fall only by buybacks (-0.9%/yr). (d) My EV/EBITDA leg's growth division was ad hoc; it now reads LTM GAAP EBITDA like the peers' trailing figures (exit 10.9x on my own EBITDA TTM 906.8), at weight 0.3 because only two peers carry it. I also fixed the interest rate (6.1% on net debt, not 5.4% of gross debt) and the Street NTM EPS in the thesis break (18.23, not 19.8). The approved drivers are unchanged; base value $313.87 (P/E $301.06, EV/EBITDA $343.75). Base rates (my lane) still shape the tails: the FY2019 analog (guide cut, -62% over 13 months, P/E trough ~10x), MasTec's Q3 2026 Communications cut and AT&T's 2027-28 capex trim (-4%) argue my central backlog view sits below the approved path (about -3% of value, for Kilian), and set the downside at backlog -12%, margins -2/-3pt, multiples -2.5 turns ($145.76). Verizon held 2026 capex at $16-16.5B, so not every carrier is cutting. Kalshi prices a 2027 recession at 20%. The upside ($493.67) stays below the peer median multiple. Horizon NTM EPS from the build, 23.3, is +8% over the Street (~21.5) because the approved drivers follow DY's beat record; the research target (12m) is +42% on a stock that fell 61%, which base rates say should be read with the caution that today's price beats every blend as a forecast. 1-month: Q3 print Nov 18-25 inside the window; ladder unchanged, near neutral.

model_inputs.gap_note: (1) Method-fit flag 'filings too thin' is an XBRL tagging gap (no market-cap/operating-income tags), not a thin business: TTM revenue 6,880 (F6) and 10+ years of filings, so multiples are not weakened and no non-multiple leg is added. (2) Judgment calls for Kilian against the approved drivers by id (not in the set): comms_ntm_backlog trimmed to FY28 +7.5% / FY29 +6% would take the research target (12m) down about 3% (round-1 sensitivity: backlog -10% in every forecast quarter = -8%; the supervisor's middle trim = -2.6%). (5) Financing: none above 20% probability found (S-3ASR shelf from 2026-03-05, no raise planned; FCF positive). (6) Horizon NTM EPS from the build is 23.32 vs Street ~21.5 (0.25 x FY28 18.98 + 0.75 x FY29 22.37, Zacks) = +8%: the approved drivers sit above consensus by DY's beat record; my base-rate prior would sit nearer the Street (carried in the downside case). comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: Exit P/E 13.2x = 29% below the 18.65x whole-company median; EV/EBITDA 10.9x = 21% below 13.85x. Both are what the k = 0.8 rule keeps of today's gap.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No extra discount beyond the k rule (an extra cut would double-count post-horizon risks the retained gap already prices). Reasons the retained discount persists: 30.5% of revenue from two carriers (AT&T 20.1%, Verizon 10.4%), a visible FTTH program end (AT&T >60M locations by 2030), net debt ~2.2x GAAP EBITDA plus debt-like supplier finance vs low-levered peers, and DY's own history of deep de-ratings after guide cuts (FY2019).
comps_summary.peer_count_flag: 7 peers (4 whole-company + 3 Building Systems segment-only). Round 1's EME EPS (34.79/39.50, StockAnalysis) is replaced by the Zacks figures (35.00/37.23 -> 18.5x), and EME is no longer mixed into the whole-company median. LMB dropped (EV ~$0.6B, one out-year estimate); IESC has no forward consensus. No other listed US/European contractor is mainly carrier fiber/wireless construction (Circet, Ervin Cable etc. are private); not padded.
